answer: All adult fibroblast subsets expressed high levels of inflammatory cytokines and receptors (e.g. IL6 and IL1RA), genes involved in antigen presentation (e.g. HLA-A), innate immune and inflammatory responses (e.g. CD55 and PTGES), and cellular senescence (CDKN1A). By contrast, prenatal skin fibroblasts had upregulated genes involved in immune suppression (CD200), regulation of inflammation (e.g. RAMP2) and tissue regeneration (MDK).
